title: Add --blocked-by, --blocks and --relates to ticket create and ticket update
description: Work in bin/heist.js only; the API already has everything: project.relations.add(sourceId, targetId, type) and project.resolveTicket(keyOrId). Direction matters: for type blocks the source is the blocker and the target is the blocked ticket. So --blocked-by X means relations.add(X, thisTicket, 'blocks'), --blocks X means relations.add(thisTicket, X, 'blocks'), --relates X means relations.add(thisTicket, X, 'relates_to'). The helper labels() in bin/heist.js already splits comma lists. Note how the argument parser names keys: a flag with a value replaces dashes with underscores, so --blocked-by arrives as opts.blocked_by. Resolve every listed ticket with project.resolveTicket before creating or updating anything, so a typo fails early. On update, catch the error with code DUPLICATE_RELATION and continue. Print one line to stderr that names what was linked, except with --format json.
why: This is the code change of the feature; the rest is documentation.

acceptance.text: Create and update write the relations with the right direction
A duplicate on update is skipped
The usage text lists the flags

todos.text: Read the ticket create and ticket update branches in bin/heist.js and the relation add branch
Write a small function that takes the ticket id and opts, resolves all listed tickets first and then adds the relations
Call it from ticket create after the ticket exists and from ticket update
Refuse a ticket that is listed in both --blocked-by and --blocks
Add the flags to the usage text next to ticket create and ticket update
Add a test to test/cli.test.js: create with each flag, check heist relation list --format json, check that an unknown key exits non-zero and creates no ticket
